findings.issue_text: [BUG] GitHubPRCommentWorkflow.get_comment_body calls self.get_merged_pr_single_issue_template(...) and self.get_environment_info(issue), but both methods are defined on CommitContextIntegration, which is not in the workflow MRO (GitHubPRCommentWorkflow -> PRCommentWorkflow -> OpenPRCommentWorkflow -> ABC). Building the body for a merged-PR comment raises AttributeError: 'GitHubPRCommentWorkflow' object has no attribute 'get_merged_pr_single_issue_template' before any comment is posted, so the GitHub PR-bot never posts merged-PR comments and every attempt errors.

[BUG] GitlabPRCommentWorkflow.get_comment_body calls self.get_merged_pr_single_issue_template(...) and self.get_environment_info(issue), but both methods are defined on CommitContextIntegration, which GitlabPRCommentWorkflow does not inherit from (its MRO is PRCommentWorkflow -> OpenPRCommentWorkflow -> ABC). Every merged-PR comment for GitLab orgs with the PR bot enabled raises AttributeError inside get_comment_body, so no comment body is ever produced and the comment-posting task fails.

[BUG] get_merged_pr_single_issue_template is added to CommitContextIntegration but internally calls PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title(title), while _truncate_title is defined on CommitContextIntegration and PRCommentWorkflow (a subclass of OpenPRCommentWorkflow(ABC)) does not inherit from CommitContextIntegration. Any invocation of get_merged_pr_single_issue_template raises AttributeError: type object 'PRCommentWorkflow' has no attribute '_truncate_title', so the merged-PR issue template can never be rendered even if the method were reachable from the workflow classes.

[BUG] The diff deletes the ParameterizationRegexExperiment class (and its __all__ entry) plus the grouping.experiments.parameterization.traceparent option registration in src/sentry/options/defaults.py, but no hunk in the diff removes the unchanged code that constructs the traceparent experiment and imports the class by name. The remaining `from sentry.grouping.parameterization import ParameterizationRegexExperiment` reference raises ImportError when the grouping experiment builder is imported, and any options.get of the now-unregistered traceparent flag raises UnknownOption, breaking event grouping at startup/ingest time.

[BUG] gen_request_data compares error_events[error_idx]["timestamp"] (copied verbatim from the nodestore event payload, where timestamp is an ISO-8601 string) against event.get("timestamp", 0) for rrweb segment events, which are numeric epoch milliseconds, using the `<` operator across mismatched types. Every summarize-breadcrumbs request for a replay with at least one error raises TypeError: '<' not supported between instances of 'str' and 'int' inside on_results, returning a 500 instead of a summary, so the new error-context feature never works on its primary path.

[BUG] fetch_error_details pairs each error_id with events.values() positionally via zip(error_ids, events.values()), but nodestore get_multi returns a dict built in backend query order with no contract that value order matches the input node-id order (the django backend assembles results from an id__in database query). For replays with multiple errors, each ErrorEvent is built from a different event's title/message than its id, and when a node is missing the shorter values() list truncates the zip so the wrong errors are silently dropped from the Seer summarization prompt.

[ADVISORY] The get handler runs query_replay_instance and process_raw_response unconditionally before evaluating the enable_error_context flag, whose only consumed output is error_ids. Every summarize-breadcrumbs request now pays an additional snuba replay-instance query that the pre-diff endpoint never issued, including requests that explicitly disable error context and derive no value from the query, adding snuba load and latency to a previously snuba-free path.

[ADVISORY] The autofix automation tuning default is hand-maintained in two independent places — DEFAULT_AUTOFIX_AUTOMATION_TUNING_DEFAULT in constants.py and the literal default in projectoptions/defaults.py's register(key="sentry:autofix_automation_tuning", default="off") — forcing this diff to make the same semantic edit in both files. The next change to the tuning default that updates only one of the two registrations leaves the org-level and project-level defaults silently disagreeing, so projects get different autofix automation behavior depending on which layer resolves the default.

[BUG] The chronological-interleave comparison compares the nodestore event timestamp — an ISO-8601 string like "2024-06-11T16:29:54.688Z" read verbatim from the raw event payload via data.get("timestamp", 0.0) at line 115 — against replay segment event timestamps, which are numeric epoch values, so the `<` raises TypeError. Every summarize-breadcrumbs request for a replay that has error_ids returns a 500 with TypeError: '<' not supported between 'str' and 'float' instead of a summary — the feature's primary use case (replays with errors) is entirely broken, and the broad try/except in fetch_error_details cannot mask it because the comparison runs later in gen_request_data.

[BUG] fetch_error_details pairs error IDs with nodestore results positionally via zip(error_ids, events.values()) instead of keying by the node_id that nodestore.backend.get_multi actually returns. get_multi returns a dict keyed by node id that omits missing nodes and follows database row order, so whenever any error event is absent from nodestore (retention-expired or purged) or rows come back out of order, each error's title/message/timestamp is attached to the wrong error ID and surviving errors are silently misattributed, feeding the Seer summary error details that describe the wrong events.

[BUG] The rewritten collector hard-rejects any report whose type is not one of the eight hardcoded BROWSER_REPORT_TYPES (ChoiceField at line 39) and returns 422 for the entire batch on the first invalid report, where the previous dataclass construction accepted any type string because Literal annotations are not enforced at runtime. Browsers delivering report types outside the list — NEL network-error reports ride the same Reporting API pipeline and the spec permits arbitrary types on named endpoints — get the whole batch (including its valid csp-violation/deprecation reports) rejected and retried with attempts incremented, so report types that were previously ingested and counted stop being recorded, and the new strictness can only be disabled via the endpoint-wide collector_endpoint_enabled kill switch.

[ADVISORY] The enable_error_context=false opt-out is evaluated only after the new query_replay_instance snuba query has already run unconditionally, so the flag suppresses just the nodestore fetch and not the error-context snuba round-trip it is named for. Clients passing enable_error_context=false to shed load still pay a snuba query per request whose result is then discarded, and the snuba+nodestore work this endpoint never performed before the diff has no server-side gate (no options entry or feature flag — only a per-request query param defaulting to enabled), so an operator cannot disable the new backend load without a code deploy.

[ADVISORY] The preprod_artifact.api.assemble analytics event is recorded before the feature gate and before any request validation, so every POST to the endpoint emits it. Requests from organizations without the organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble feature (403) and requests that fail payload validation are counted as assemble events, so adoption/usage dashboards for the preprod artifact feature overcount and cannot distinguish real assembles from denied or malformed requests.

[ADVISORY] The interleave comparison mixes timestamp units — event-payload timestamps are epoch seconds while replay segment (rrweb-format) event timestamps are epoch milliseconds — and the diff normalizes neither type nor unit. Once the string-vs-number crash is fixed, every error timestamp still compares as 1000x smaller than every segment event timestamp, so all error messages are yielded before the first breadcrumb and the chronological interleaving the feature exists to produce collapses into an errors-first list, handing Seer a misleading narrative.

[ADVISORY] The owner-to-(owner_user_id, owner_team_id) resolution policy is implemented twice — once mutating instance fields in update() (lines 66-79) and once building locals in create() (lines 120-127) — with no shared helper. The next change to owner policy (for example validating the actor belongs to the detector's organization) must be replicated in both blocks or create and update silently diverge, and the two implementations already differ in shape (instance-mutation with explicit opposite-column clearing vs. local variables), which is drift bait for the developer who touches detector ownership next.

[ADVISORY] The stated intent ('Replays Self-Serve Bulk Delete System') is not implemented by this artifact: the backend portion of the diff contains no self-serve delete API, no bulk-delete orchestration, and no authorization surface, leaving a null-guard inside the retention-delete filename builder as the only change traceable to the title. A reviewer approving this PR as the Replays bulk-delete system is approving no such system — the promised feature cannot be verified, tested, or rolled back from this diff, while roughly twenty unrelated workstreams merge under the same approval.

[BUG] get_merged_pr_single_issue_template is defined on CommitContextIntegration but resolves _truncate_title through PRCommentWorkflow, and the GitHub/GitLab workflows invoke self.get_environment_info and self.get_merged_pr_single_issue_template — none of which exist on PRCommentWorkflow, which composes an integration (OpenPRCommentWorkflow.__init__ takes a CommitContextIntegration) rather than inheriting one. Every merged-PR comment render for GitHub and GitLab raises AttributeError, so the PR bot stops posting comments entirely once this ships.

Every organization without an explicit override stops running autofix automatically on new issues the moment this deploys, and the change escapes the autofix team's rollout and revert planning because it ships inside a Replays PR.

[ADVISORY] Removes the exported ParameterizationRegexExperiment class, the isinstance dispatch in Parameterizer.run, and the grouping.experiments.parameterization.traceparent option registration (src/sentry/options/defaults.py:2624-2629) — grouping-engine changes untraceable to Replays bulk delete. [ADVISORY] Redesigns merged-PR bot comments — centralized template with environment suffix and 50-char title truncation, wired into src/sentry/integrations/github/integration.py:406 and src/sentry/integrations/gitlab/integration.py:252 — a user-facing integrations change untraceable to Replays bulk delete. GitHub and GitLab PR-bot comment output changes for every user of the feature without the integrations team reviewing it, and reverting the Replays work silently rolls back the comment redesign with it.

[ADVISORY] Replaces the BrowserReport dataclass with a DRF serializer that changes the collector's acceptance contract — age-only reports now succeed instead of raising TypeError, while reports with attempts<1, invalid URLs, or both age and timestamp now return 422 with error bodies — untraceable to Replays bulk delete. The live browser-reporting endpoint's validation semantics change under a Replays PR title, so issues-domain owners never review the new contract and clients sending previously-accepted payloads begin receiving 422s.

[ADVISORY] Adds noise_config = NoiseConfig(ignore_limit=5) to DBQueryInjectionVulnerabilityGroupType, changing issue-creation thresholds for a security group type, untraceable to the stated intent. [ADVISORY] Neuters the already-shipped 0917 and 0920 org-saved-search conversion migrations to bare returns, migration-history surgery untraceable to Replays bulk delete. Environments that recorded or applied 0917/0920 diverge from fresh installs running the emptied bodies, and anyone debugging saved-search view conversions or reverting this PR gets inconsistent migration state — a change needing release-engineer scrutiny a Replays-titled review never gives it.

[ADVISORY] Builds a new error-context capability for replay breadcrumb summarization — an unconditional Snuba replay-instance query plus nodestore multi-get before pagination, with chronological error interleaving — Replays-domain work that serves the summarize feature, not the stated bulk-delete intent. The summarize endpoint gains two new remote round-trips on every request where it previously only paginated segment metadata, so latency and failure modes of a different feature change under a bulk-delete title, and reverting the delete work drags this feature along.

[BUG] fetch_error_details builds ErrorEvent.timestamp from raw nodestore event data, where timestamp is an ISO-8601 string, and gen_request_data then compares it with '<' against the numeric timestamps of replay-segment events. The comparison raises TypeError and the summarize request 500s whenever error context is present — the feature's primary path — instead of returning a summary.

[ADVISORY] Adds an owner ActorField with user/team resolution to detector create and update, new workflow-engine API behavior untraceable to Replays bulk delete. The detector API contract gains owner assignment semantics without workflow-engine owners reviewing it under this title, and any contract mistake ships bundled with — and reverts with — the Replays work.

[ADVISORY] The new null-guard treats max_segment_id is None as proof that no recording segments exist and returns [] without verifying, so the delete path's invariant — that a deleted replay leaves no segment files behind — is enforced by assumption alone. Any replay whose segments were ingested while max_segment_id stayed null (pre-existing rows, ingest races, ClickHouse/Postgres drift) has all its recording segment files silently retained forever, violating the deletion guarantee the bulk-delete system exists to provide, with no error, metric, or audit trail.

[ADVISORY] Rewrites the feedback-summaries LLM prompt and input joining ('\n------\n' separators, 55-word hard cap, new anti-genericity instructions), work untraceable to the stated intent. Live AI summarization output changes under a Replays-delete title, so feedback-summary regressions cannot be bisected to this PR and the prompt change is never reviewed by the feedback/Seer feature owners.

[ADVISORY] Adds taskworker processing_deadline_duration limits (30s here, 300s at :161, 120s at :239, and 60s in src/sentry/tasks/auth/check_auth.py:76) to webhook and auth tasks, untraceable to the stated intent. Webhook mailbox drains that legitimately exceed the new deadlines are now killed and retried, an operational change to delivery infrastructure that ships unreviewed inside a Replays PR and is unrevertable independently of it.

[ADVISORY] Adds a new preprod_artifact.api.assemble analytics event (src/sentry/preprod/analytics.py) and records it before the feature-gate check, work untraceable to Replays bulk delete. [ADVISORY] Adds an equations parameter to run_top_events_timeseries_query that no caller in this diff passes, untraceable to Replays bulk delete. The logs-dataset query API surface changes for the logs/analytics team with no visible consumer in the artifact, shipping speculative surface inside a Replays PR.

[ADVISORY] Refactors delayed-workflow slow-condition handling — hoisting get_slow_conditions_for_groups into process_delayed_workflows, threading dcg_to_slow_conditions through get_condition_query_groups and get_groups_to_fire, adding a no-slow-conditions log, and swapping the logger in processors/workflow.py:35 — untraceable to the stated intent. Workflow-engine processing and observability semantics change under a Replays title, so any delayed-workflow regression becomes unattributable to the code that caused it and reverts of the Replays work roll this back unnoticed.

[ADVISORY] Removes the 'Type' row and its explanatory QuestionTooltip from every grouping-variant display case, a user-facing UX removal untraceable to Replays bulk delete. Users lose the per-type grouping explanations in the grouping-info UI, and the removal ships without the grouping/UI owners ever reviewing a 'Replays delete' PR.

[ADVISORY] Changes the chonk button hover transition from 0.1s to 0.06s, a design-system-wide animation change untraceable to Replays bulk delete. Every chonk button in the app animates differently once this deploys — a design-system change that ships without design-system owners reviewing it and that a revert of the Replays work would silently roll back.

[ADVISORY] Stands up a complete tracing dev environment — a snuba-metrics service (:23-29), four subscription-results consumers (:131-140 and :325-332), and a 20-service 'tracing' mode — untraceable to Replays bulk delete. Every developer's devservices topology changes under a Replays PR, and reverting the Replays work deletes colleagues' tracing dev environment along with it.

[BUG] `get_merged_pr_single_issue_template` is added to `CommitContextIntegration` but its body calls `PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title`, while `_truncate_title` (line 577) is defined on `CommitContextIntegration` — `PRCommentWorkflow` is a workflow class that receives a `CommitContextIntegration` instance in `OpenPRCommentWorkflow.__init__` and does not inherit from it, so the attribute does not exist on `PRCommentWorkflow`. Building any merged-PR comment body raises AttributeError (`type object 'PRCommentWorkflow' has no attribute '_truncate_title'`), so the merged-PR comment feature crashes for every provider instead of posting the comment.

[BUG] `GitHubPRCommentWorkflow.get_comment_body` calls `self.get_merged_pr_single_issue_template(...)` and `self.get_environment_info(issue)`, but both helpers are defined on `CommitContextIntegration` (commit_context.py lines 584-606); the workflow composes an integration via `self.integration` rather than inheriting `CommitContextIntegration`, so the methods are not on the workflow hierarchy. Every merged-PR comment for GitHub raises AttributeError while constructing the comment body, so comments are never posted and the comment workflow task fails.

[BUG] `GitlabPRCommentWorkflow.get_comment_body` calls `self.get_merged_pr_single_issue_template(...)` and `self.get_environment_info(issue)`, but both helpers are defined on `CommitContextIntegration`, which the workflow holds via `self.integration` and does not inherit. Every merged-PR comment for GitLab raises AttributeError while constructing the comment body, so comments are never posted and the comment workflow task fails.

[BUG] `fetch_error_details` pairs error ids to event data positionally via `zip(error_ids, events.values())`, but `nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` returns a dict keyed by node_id whose iteration order follows the bulk query's return order (not the input order) and that omits missing node ids entirely on bulk-query backends, so the code pairs by position against an unordered, partially-filled mapping instead of by key (`events.get(node_id)`). When any error event's node is missing from nodestore (retention-expired or never written) or the backend returns rows out of input order, each error_id is paired with the wrong event's title/message/timestamp — the summary attributes error X's details to error Y — and the `if data is not None` guard never filters anything because missing keys are absent rather than None.

[BUG] `gen_request_data` compares nodestore error timestamps (epoch seconds, e.g. 1712345678.123) against rrweb segment event timestamps (epoch milliseconds, e.g. 1712345678123) in `error_events[error_idx]['timestamp'] < event.get('timestamp', 0)`, mixing units in the ordering comparison. Every error timestamp in seconds compares as strictly less than every breadcrumb timestamp in milliseconds, so the while-loop drains all error messages before the first breadcrumb event — the chronological interleaving this function exists to produce never happens, and the Seer prompt receives every error positioned at the session start regardless of when it actually occurred.

[BUG] `owner = ActorField(required=False, allow_null=True)` is added to `BaseDetectorTypeValidator`, but sentry's `ActorField.to_internal_value` requires `organization` in the serializer context and raises RuntimeError when it is absent, and this validator's context is only ever read for `project` and `request` — no organization is passed or read anywhere in the file. Any detector create or update request that includes the new `owner` field raises RuntimeError('Organization is required context for ActorField') and returns a 500 instead of creating or updating the detector.

[BUG] The age/timestamp validators enforce mutual exclusion via truthiness (`if self.initial_data.get('age')`) and both fields are `required=False`, so a report carrying `age: 0` together with a `timestamp` passes validation and a report carrying neither field passes as well — contradicting the docstrings' claims that 'timestamp must be present' and 'age must be present'. Reports that violate the Reporting API shape (both fields set, or neither) are accepted and counted in the collector metrics, so the guard added to enforce 'exactly one of age/timestamp' does not enforce it and malformed reports flow through the endpoint undetected.

[ADVISORY] Validation is all-or-nothing per batch — one invalid report returns 422 for the entire array — and `type` is a closed ChoiceField over a hardcoded list of report types that browsers, not this server, control and extend over time. When a browser ships a report type outside BROWSER_REPORT_TYPES, every batch containing it is rejected with 422; per the Reporting API the browser retries and then drops/deprioritizes the endpoint on repeated non-2xx, so collection silently stops for affected browsers and the metrics this endpoint exists to gather vanish.

[ADVISORY] The endpoint's error-context feature reads `error_ids` from `process_raw_response(snuba_response, fields=request.query_params.getlist('field'))`, so the column is only present when the client happens to include `error_ids` in its `field` query params — the endpoint never requests it server-side. Every caller that does not send `field` including `error_ids` silently receives breadcrumb-only summaries with no error context and no error surfaced, leaving the new capability inert for any client not passing the param.

[ADVISORY] The `preprod_artifact.api.assemble` analytics event is recorded before the `features.has` gate, so feature-denied requests are emitted as assemble events with no outcome attribute distinguishing them from successful ones. Anyone reading this analytics metric overcounts adoption — 403-denied requests are indistinguishable from real assembles — and the event fires for organizations that do not have the feature at all, skewing the data the event was added to collect.

[ADVISORY] The `sentry:autofix_automation_tuning` default flips from 'low' to 'off' with no backfill, migration, or per-project opt-in, so every project that never explicitly set the option changes behavior at deploy time. All existing projects relying on the implicit default silently lose automatic autofix runs on new issues — a feature reduction applied to every default-relying project at once with no notification path.

[ADVISORY] The same autofix tuning default is hand-maintained as a literal in two places — `DEFAULT_AUTOFIX_AUTOMATION_TUNING_DEFAULT` in constants.py and the `register(...)` default in projectoptions/defaults.py — with nothing linking them; this diff must update both in lockstep to keep them equal. The next editor who changes one copy but not the other silently diverges the constant from the project-option default, and projects observe different defaults depending on which code path reads which copy.

[BUG] DEFAULT_AUTOFIX_AUTOMATION_TUNING_DEFAULT is flipped from "low" to "off" inside a PR whose stated objective is the replays bulk delete system, silently changing the shipped default for autofix automation with no backfill migration or feature flag anywhere in the artifact. Every organization that never explicitly set the autofix automation tuning option loses automatically-running autofix on new issues the moment this deploys, because the previously accepted "low" default is replaced at read time with no acceptance trail for existing users.

[BUG] The sentry:autofix_automation_tuning project option default is flipped from "low" to "off", silently disabling autofix automation for every project that relied on the implicit default. Existing projects with no explicit option row stop running autofix automatically on new issues after deploy; users experience silent feature loss with no migration preserving the previously accepted "low" behavior.

[ADVISORY] DBQueryInjectionVulnerabilityGroupType silently gains noise_config = NoiseConfig(ignore_limit=5), changing a security issue type's alerting contract from immediate surfacing to suppression until 5 occurrences, buried in an unrelated PR with no flag or acceptance trail. Users relying on prompt notification of DB query injection findings have the first occurrences archived/ignored without notification, and the security detector's contract changes for all existing projects the moment this ships.

[BUG] get_merged_pr_single_issue_template and get_environment_info are defined on CommitContextIntegration but invoked as self.get_merged_pr_single_issue_template/self.get_environment_info from GitHubPRCommentWorkflow and GitlabPRCommentWorkflow, whose MRO (PRCommentWorkflow → OpenPRCommentWorkflow, which holds the integration via composition as self.integration) does not include CommitContextIntegration, and the staticmethod itself calls PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title, a method defined on CommitContextIntegration rather than PRCommentWorkflow. Generating a merged-PR comment body raises AttributeError ('GitHubPRCommentWorkflow' object has no attribute 'get_merged_pr_single_issue_template'), so suspect-issue comments on merged PRs are never posted for GitHub and GitLab.

[BUG] gen_request_data compares error_events[error_idx]["timestamp"] — populated from nodestore event data where timestamp is an ISO-8601 string — against replay segment event timestamps, which are numeric epoch values, so the < comparison raises TypeError. Any summarize request for a replay that has both error events and breadcrumb events crashes with TypeError and returns a 500 instead of the summary, breaking the new error-context feature on its primary path (it only works for replays with no errors).

[BUG] The age/timestamp validators enforce only falsy-based mutual exclusion: both fields are required=False so a report containing neither temporal field passes validation, and age=0 (a legitimate, common value) bypasses the exclusion check because self.initial_data.get("age") is falsy. Spec-invalid reports (no age and no timestamp, or age=0 alongside timestamp) are accepted into validated_reports and counted in browser_reporting.raw_report_received, so the validation layer fails the contract its own docstrings and the referenced Reporting API specs state, and any future consumer of validated_data inherits silently malformed data.

[ADVISORY] The serializer requires user_agent, destination, and attempts — fields that exist only in the Editor's Draft report format — so Working Draft reports (type/url/age/body) are rejected with 422 despite the in-diff comment "We need to support both" specs. Reports from browsers emitting the Working Draft format are never collected (the whole batch is rejected and the browser retries then discards), so the artifact does not deliver the both-specs intent it explicitly states and the collected metrics undercount real browser traffic.

[ADVISORY] The summarize-breadcrumbs GET silently gains an unconditional Snuba query_replay_instance call plus a nodestore get_multi on every request, with the new behavior defaulting on and controllable only by the client-supplied enable_error_context query param — no feature flag or options entry gates it server-side. A Snuba failure or timeout now 500s an endpoint that previously served from segment storage alone, and operators cannot disable the new remote dependency without a code deploy; the endpoint's execution contract changed with no acceptance trail in the artifact.

[BUG] fetch_error_details pairs error IDs with nodestore results positionally via zip(error_ids, events.values()) instead of keying by node ID, so whenever get_multi omits missing keys or returns them in non-input order (the django nodestore backend builds its mapping from a DB query, and expired/deleted error events are common for older replays) the values shift relative to the IDs. Error titles, messages, and timestamps are attributed to the wrong event IDs and trailing errors are silently dropped, so the generated summary interleaves the wrong errors at the wrong points in the replay timeline.

[ADVISORY] Removing the ParameterizationRegexExperiment dispatch branch orphans the module-level _handle_regex_match callback, whose only call site was the deleted else-branch, while ParameterizationRegex remains exported in __all__ with no remaining instantiation in the diff. Maintainers of the grouping parameterization path must preserve and reason about a regex-matching callback that can no longer execute, and the next change to this file risks updating or "restoring" dead logic; deleting the callback and the now-unreachable regex path is the safer state.

[BUG] get_merged_pr_single_issue_template interpolates the event-supplied issue title and the new environment name (built unescaped at line 590 as f" in `{environment.name}`") directly into the GitHub/GitLab markdown comment template with no markdown escaping, so untrusted content breaks out of the link structure and injects arbitrary markdown into PR comments. Anyone who can send events to the project (browser/mobile SDK DSNs are public, and error titles routinely embed end-user-controlled input) crafts a title or environment name containing `](https://phish.example)` or `@mentions` — the merged-PR bot then renders attacker-chosen links, images, and mentions inside the org's own repositories under the trusted integration identity, a phishing/spoofing vector; the environment interpolation is a new injection point introduced by this diff.

[ADVISORY] The new browser_report_validation_failed warning logs the raw, unvalidated report body from an endpoint declared with permission_classes = () plus CSRF exemption and open CORS, handing unauthenticated clients a direct write-into-logs primitive. When the collector option is enabled, any internet client (not just browsers — nothing authenticates the POST) can flood Sentry's log pipeline with arbitrary content at warning level (log-storage DoS and cost amplification, since each invalid report is logged verbatim), and the logged report.url fields persist full page URLs — which in many apps carry session tokens or password-reset parameters — into log storage; the pre-existing browser_report_received info log has the same flaw and this diff adds a second raw-body sink instead of bounding it.

[ADVISORY] The new owner field resolves a user-supplied actor id via ActorField and writes it straight to owner_user_id/owner_team_id in both create() (lines 120-127) and update() (lines 66-79) with no organization-membership validation anywhere in the validator. A user with detector write access in one organization sets the detector owner to any user or team id resolvable from the global actor table — including actors belonging to other organizations — so owner-based display, assignment, and notification routing target a foreign actor, breaking the org-scoped ownership invariant and potentially routing detector/issue notifications to a user who is not a member of the org.

Any code path that builds a merged-PR issue comment line crashes with AttributeError before the template string is ever produced, so the reformatted comment body cannot be generated at all.

Building the body for a merged-PR bot comment raises AttributeError ('GitHubPRCommentWorkflow' object has no attribute 'get_merged_pr_single_issue_template'), so organizations with sentry:github_pr_bot enabled never receive merged-PR comments and the posting task errors on every attempt.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] `fetch_error_details` pairs error ids to event data positionally via `zip(error_ids, events.values())`, but `nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` returns a dict keyed by node_id whose iteration order follows the bulk query's return order (not the input order) and that omits missing node ids entirely on bulk-query backends, so the code pairs by position against an unordered, partially-filled mapping instead of by key (`events.get(node_id)`). When any error event's node is missing from nodestore (retention-expired or never written) or the backend returns rows out of input order, each error_id is paired with the wrong event's title/message/timestamp — the summary attributes error X's details to error Y — and the `if data is not None` guard never filters anything because missing keys are absent rather than None.

adjudication.rationale: In `fetch_error_details` (new in `project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py`), the code does `events = nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` and then builds `ErrorEvent`s via `for event_id, data in zip(error_ids, events.values())`. This pairs IDs with values by positional iteration over a dict, not by the corresponding `node_id` key. If `get_multi` returns a mapping that does not include entries for missing node_ids (common for bulk-get APIs), `events.values()` will be shorter and `zip` will misattribute later returned event data to earlier missing `error_id`s (and `zip` will also truncate). Even if all exist, relying on dict value iteration order to match `error_ids` is brittle; the safe approach is to iterate `error_ids/node_ids` and look up `events.get(node_id)`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] `gen_request_data` compares nodestore error timestamps (epoch seconds, e.g. 1712345678.123) against rrweb segment event timestamps (epoch milliseconds, e.g. 1712345678123) in `error_events[error_idx]['timestamp'] < event.get('timestamp', 0)`, mixing units in the ordering comparison. Every error timestamp in seconds compares as strictly less than every breadcrumb timestamp in milliseconds, so the while-loop drains all error messages before the first breadcrumb event — the chronological interleaving this function exists to produce never happens, and the Seer prompt receives every error positioned at the session start regardless of when it actually occurred.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] BrowserReportSerializer declares both age and timestamp as required=False and enforces only mutual exclusion, so a report containing neither field passes validation even though the validators' own docstrings (and both cited specs) require exactly one of them to be present. Spec-violating reports with neither age nor timestamp are accepted with HTTP 200 and counted in the browser_reporting.raw_report_received metric, so the metric overcounts valid reports and the one-of contract the new validation claims to implement is not enforced.

adjudication.rationale: In `BrowserReportSerializer` (`src/sentry/issues/endpoints/browser_reporting_collector.py`), both `age` and `timestamp` are `required=False`, and the only validation implemented is mutual exclusion via `validate_timestamp`/`validate_age`. Those validators only error when the *other* field is present (`self.initial_data.get("age")` / `self.initial_data.get("timestamp")`) and do not enforce that at least one of them must be provided. Therefore a report with neither `age` nor `timestamp` will pass `serializer.is_valid()`, return HTTP 200, and increment `browser_reporting.raw_report_received`, matching the finding’s claim that spec-violating reports are accepted and counted.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] fetch_error_details copies the nodestore event's ISO-8601 string timestamp into ErrorEvent via `timestamp=data.get("timestamp", 0.0)` (line 115), and gen_request_data then compares that string against rrWeb's numeric segment timestamps with `error_events[error_idx]["timestamp"] < event.get("timestamp", 0)`, which raises TypeError in Python 3 (the same mixed-type comparison also breaks the sort at line 138 when any event lacks a timestamp). Every summarize-breadcrumbs request for a replay that has both error events and recording segments crashes with TypeError ('<' not supported between 'str' and 'int') inside paginate's on_results and returns a 500 — the endpoint's primary path is broken on arrival; even if the types were coerced, event timestamps are epoch seconds while rrWeb timestamps are epoch milliseconds, so errors would silently misorder against breadcrumbs in the Seer prompt.

adjudication.rationale: In `fetch_error_details`, `timestamp` is taken verbatim from nodestore (`timestamp=data.get("timestamp", 0.0)`) and stored into `ErrorEvent` without coercion. Later, `get_request_data` sorts `error_events` by `x["timestamp"]` and `gen_request_data` does an ordering comparison `error_events[error_idx]["timestamp"] < event.get("timestamp", 0)`. If the nodestore event payload’s `timestamp` is a string (common in Sentry event JSON) while replay segment events use numeric timestamps, this will raise a Python 3 `TypeError` at runtime. The diff contains no normalization to a numeric epoch, so the mixed-type comparison/sort is a real defect risk introduced by the new error-context logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The query_replay_instance snuba query (lines 70-77) runs unconditionally before the enable_error_context=false kill-switch is evaluated (lines 87-94), and its processed response is consumed solely to extract error_ids for fetch_error_details, so requests that disable error context still pay a full snuba replay-instance query that this endpoint never made before the diff. Clients hitting the endpoint with error context disabled (and every summarize request generally) still incur a new per-request snuba query on a path that previously served from segment storage alone, adding latency and snuba load that the disable flag was meant to avoid.

adjudication.rationale: In `ProjectReplaySummarizeBreadcrumbsEndpoint.get`, the code always computes `filter_params`, calls `query_replay_instance(...)`, and runs `process_raw_response(...)` to derive `error_ids` before checking `enable_error_context` (kill-switch) and potentially skipping `fetch_error_details` (see the new block starting with `snuba_response = query_replay_instance(...)` and the later `disable_error_fetching = ...`). Therefore requests with `enable_error_context=false` still incur the extra Snuba query and response processing overhead, which is a real diff-grounded performance/latency concern rather than a functional correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] get_environment_info performs an eventstore/nodestore recommended-event fetch (issue.get_recommended_event(), line 586) plus environment resolution per issue, and it is invoked inside the per-issue list comprehension in GitHubPRCommentWorkflow/GitlabPRCommentWorkflow.get_comment_body, replacing the previous zero-remote-call read of issue.culprit from the already-loaded Group row. Merged-PR comment generation now issues one recommended-event lookup per linked issue on a path that previously made no remote calls, so orgs with the PR bot enabled see comment-posting latency and nodestore load that scale with the number of issues linked to a PR.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `CommitContextIntegration.get_environment_info()` which calls `issue.get_recommended_event()` and then `recommended_event.get_environment()`, and `GitHubPRCommentWorkflow.get_comment_body` / `GitlabPRCommentWorkflow.get_comment_body` now invoke it inside the per-issue list comprehension (`environment=self.get_environment_info(issue)`). Previously the template used `issue.culprit` from the already-loaded `Group`. While the diff doesn’t prove the exact backend cost of `get_recommended_event()`, it clearly introduces an extra per-issue fetch/lookup on the merged-PR comment path, so latency/load can now scale with issue count.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] gen_request_data compares nodestore error timestamps (float seconds from event data, via data.get("timestamp", 0.0)) directly against rrweb segment event timestamps (milliseconds, via event.get("timestamp", 0)) with `<`, so for any post-1970 replay the error timestamp is always numerically smaller and every error message is yielded before the first breadcrumb event. The chronological interleaving this diff implements never happens: Seer receives all error lines clustered at the top of the log list regardless of when the errors actually occurred, silently degrading every replay breadcrumb summary that includes errors.

adjudication.rationale: The new interleaving logic in `gen_request_data` compares `error_events[...]["timestamp"]` (from nodestore `data.get("timestamp", 0.0)`) against segment `event.get("timestamp", 0)` with no unit conversion. However, the diff itself does not establish that replay segment event timestamps are milliseconds. In fact, the added tests construct segment events using `float(now.timestamp())` (seconds since epoch) and expect correct chronological interleaving (e.g., 1.0/1.5/2.0/3.0), which would fail if timestamps were ms-vs-s. So the claim that errors will always sort before breadcrumbs for real replays is not verifiable from this PR diff and is contradicted by the test data/expectations included here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The serializer requires user_agent, destination, and attempts — fields that exist only in the Editor's Draft report format — so Working Draft reports (type/age/url/body only, per the spec the class-level comment cites and claims to support) always fail validation with 422. Any browser or webview emitting the Working Draft format has 100% of its reports rejected and dropped (the browser retries the batch a few times, then gives up), so the collector loses an entire class of reports whenever the endpoint is enabled; the age field added for Working Draft support can never validate on a real Working Draft report.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `BrowserReportSerializer` explicitly treats only `age` vs `timestamp` as spec-differentiating fields (both optional and mutually exclusive via `validate_timestamp`/`validate_age`). The required fields (`body`, `type`, `url`, `user_agent`, `destination`, `attempts`) are assumed to exist in both formats, and the added tests demonstrate that a “Working Draft” example containing `timestamp`+`user_agent`+`destination`+`attempts` validates (200), while an “Editor’s Draft” example containing `age` (and also `user_agent`/`destination`/`attempts`) also validates (200). There is no evidence in the diff that Working Draft reports are expected to omit `user_agent`/`destination`/`attempts`, nor that `age` can never validate—`INTERVENTION_REPORT` uses `age` successfully.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] validate_timestamp and validate_age enforce the age/timestamp mutual exclusion with truthiness checks (`if self.initial_data.get("age")` / `if self.initial_data.get("timestamp")`), so age=0 and timestamp=0 — both in-domain, timestamp explicitly declares min_value=0 — are treated as absent and a report carrying both zero values bypasses the either-or validation (a report carrying neither passes too, since both fields are required=False). Spec-violating reports are accepted with a 200 and counted in browser_reporting.raw_report_received, so the validation the serializer exists to enforce silently passes and the metric over-counts malformed reports.
matched_golden_ids: Validation logic incorrectly uses .get('timestamp'), which treats a timestamp of 0 as absent. It should directly check 'timestamp' in self.initial_data to ensure proper field presence detection, preventing both 'age=0' and 'timestamp' from passing mutual-exclusion validation.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same root bug: using `self.initial_data.get(...)`/truthiness checks causes a value of 0 (valid for timestamp and potentially for age) to be treated as missing, allowing mutual-exclusion validation to be bypassed. This aligns with the golden comment’s point that presence should be checked via key membership (e.g., `'timestamp' in self.initial_data`) rather than `.get()`/truthiness.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] fetch_error_details pairs error_ids with nodestore results positionally via `zip(error_ids, events.values())`, but get_multi returns a dict keyed by node_id that omits missing keys and need not preserve input order (the django backend returns only found rows in query order), so whenever a node is missing or reordered the ErrorEvent is built with a different error's id and data. ErrorEvent.id is misattributed to the wrong error whenever any node is absent or the backend reorders results — latent today because only title/message/timestamp reach the log message, but any consumer of the id (e.g., deep-linking an error out of a summary) points at the wrong event; on the django nodestore backend this triggers whenever any error node has been cleaned up while others remain.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py`, `fetch_error_details` does `events = nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` and then builds `ErrorEvent` objects by iterating `zip(error_ids, events.values())`. Since `get_multi` returns a dict keyed by node_id and may omit missing keys and/or not preserve the same positional order as `node_ids`, pairing by `events.values()` can misassociate an `event_id` from `error_ids` with a different event's data whenever any node is missing or returned in a different order. This logic is newly introduced by the diff, so the defect is introduced/exposed here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The endpoint executes query_replay_instance and process_raw_response unconditionally, and the enable_error_context=false branch only skips fetch_error_details, so the Snuba query whose sole consumer is the discarded error_ids still runs for requests that explicitly disabled error context. Clients opting out of error context still pay a Snuba round-trip per summarize request, and when Snuba is degraded or slow those requests still fail with a 500 even though the client disabled the only feature that needs Snuba.

adjudication.rationale: In `ProjectReplaySummarizeBreadcrumbsEndpoint.get`, the code always computes `filter_params`, calls `query_replay_instance(...)`, and then `process_raw_response(...)` to derive `error_ids` before checking `enable_error_context` (see the new block before `disable_error_fetching`). When `enable_error_context=false`, it sets `error_events = []` and never uses `error_ids`, so that Snuba round-trip becomes unnecessary overhead and also makes the request depend on Snuba even when the caller explicitly disabled error context. The claim about potential 500s is plausible since there is no try/except around `query_replay_instance`/`process_raw_response`, but the diff doesn’t show the exact exception behavior of those functions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] analytics.record('preprod_artifact.api.assemble') fires before the feature-flag check and before any payload validation, so requests the gate rejects are recorded as assemble events. Whoever consumes the preprod_artifact.api.assemble metric sees gated-out and malformed requests counted as feature usage with no attribute to separate them, overstating adoption of the assemble feature.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/preprod/api/endpoints/organization_preprod_artifact_assemble.py`, the diff adds `analytics.record("preprod_artifact.api.assemble", ...)` at the very start of `post()`, before the subsequent feature-flag gate `features.has("organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble", ...)`. This means requests that are rejected by the feature check will still be counted as assemble events, which can overstate feature adoption in downstream analytics. The diff does not show any payload validation before the record either (the record happens immediately upon entering the handler).
